adaptation: نجيب لك الخير لين بابك.. حرفياً.
back_translation: We bring the goodness (bounty) right to your door... literally.
notes: The English idiom 'deliver the goods' has no Arabic equivalent, so the wordplay now rests on 'الخير', which in Saudi usage means both blessing/goodness and food provisions, and the line uses warm Saudi dialect ('نجيب لك', 'لين بابك') to sound local and hospitable.
